doc.title: Mike Davis interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, April 1, 2024

title: 'A Life Lived' and 'Stomper': tune stories
summary: Davis explains the 9/11 memorial for six trombones and the Oakland A's mascot tune, and how titles shape music.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

And then kind of the third way would be dealing with the rhythmic element first and that’s going to create a different approach to how you’re going to write the melody. So I think I just kind of roll with whatever happens on that. The two tunes that you are referencing, “Life Lived” is a composition for six trombones that I wrote for a record I did called “New Brass.” And yeah, it’s exactly, it was a dedication to victims of 9/11. So you know that kind of has an implication about what kind of music that’s going to be. It’s kind of somber and in memoriam of that horrible day. “Stomper” is — I wanted to do something on a record I did called “Absolute Trombone II” that was for six trombones and drums. No bass or piano. And “Stomper,” I kept all my Bay Area teams so I’m a big Oakland A’s fan which is really really hard to do right now. But “Stomper” is the mascot of the A’s. So my youngest son Zack, who is a trumpet player, he became a big A’s fan. I think he just liked the colors, I’m not really sure why, when he was two years old he just — so we would always go to an A’s game when they’re in New York and sometimes in other cities as well and we would see this character “Stomper” which is an elephant which is back from the Connie Mack era when they were the Philadelphia Athletics. So that gives you a different kind of, you know, conjures up something else, like the music from “Life Lived” wouldn’t work well with the title “Stomper.”
Yes, you answered my question about titles.
